segments.title: Chương 223: 0223【Wiki】
segments.content:
Chapter 226 Section 0223: Witkey. The level of tolerance for online speech in 2006 was frighteningly high.

In such an environment, for the editor-in-chief to deem something too sensitive meant it was more than just a simple complaint.

ByteDance's editorial and technical teams began to jointly develop a "graylist" system. Accounts that triggered sensitive words multiple times over several days would be automatically added to the "graylist" and then be subject to manual review.

The "graylist" consisted of sensitive accounts. The website would not interfere too much, striving to protect the users' freedom of speech. But editors would pay close attention to these accounts, and once their speech clearly crossed the line, they would be warned.

If they ignored multiple warnings, they would be moved to the "blacklist."

"Blacklisted" users were regulars for the post-deletion and account-suspension package. The ultimate punishment for crossing the bottom line was a permanent ban!

This process was laborious to implement, but such a rule was necessary.

China's first commercial microblogging product, Fanfou, was shut down precisely because it contained a large amount of illegal content.

Wouldn't it be easier to just suspend or ban accounts directly after a problem arises?

But doing so would lack a unified standard.

It would either end up with reviewers acting on a whim, or with anyone reported by astroturfers (or fans) getting suspended.

No matter how much Chen Guiliang disliked someone, he wouldn't arbitrarily suspend or ban their account. As long as they didn't cross legal or moral boundaries, he would respect their freedom of speech.

Public opinion is a tricky thing. It can't be all negative, nor can it be all positive.

When everyone sings the same tune and public opinion becomes uniform, it is actually very frightening and extremely dangerous. You can't tell if the person on the other side is a human or a ghost. It's like when the demon king Mara said to the Buddha: "I will have my descendants mix in with your Sangha, wear your robes, and corrupt your Dharma!"

Moreover, during this period in China, public intellectuals were also very useful. They were an important force for public supervision.

What's more, some were true "public intellectuals" who genuinely hoped China would become better. It was understandable if their speech was occasionally excessive. Even Chen Guiliang often felt like cursing after reading the news.

"You can't make this thing work!" Guo Feng walked into Chen Guiliang's office.

Chen Guiliang asked, "What thing?"

"Splitting the hot search into two lists," Guo Feng said. "Things like the Hot Visit list and the Hot Read list can be divided into two lists for verified and non-verified users. But how do you split the hot search?"

Chen Guiliang thought for a moment, "Then we won't split the hot search list."

Xie Yang also walked in. "I don't think 'Anonymous List' is appropriate. It should be changed to the 'Grassroots List,' corresponding to the verified 'Celebrity List'."

"Won't the 'Grassroots List' be misinterpreted as discriminatory?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Xie Yang said, "It won't. Grassroots culture is on the rise now, and netizens love to call themselves grassroots. If someone feels good about themselves and doesn't like the term 'grassroots,' they can choose to get verified."

Chen Guiliang considered it carefully. "The confrontational tone between the Celebrity List and the Grassroots List is too strong. Change it to the Big V List and the Grassroots List."

"That works too." Xie Yang thought it was a good idea.

Chen Guiliang said, "Let's try it out for now. You two are in charge of the specific implementation and operation. Nothing is set in stone, and not everything I say is correct. Make adjustments based on the actual operational situation."

This way, the hot search list, which didn't differentiate between Big Vs and grassroots, would likely garner the most attention. The price for buying a spot on the hot search ranking would also be the most expensive!

For all other lists, Big Vs would be grouped into one, and grassroots users in another.

Rankings on the Big V list could be bought, because even if ByteDance didn't sell them, certain people could hire astroturfers or mobilize fans to boost their rankings.

The Grassroots List, however, would be completely authentic, and ordinary users could make the list without spending any money. As long as a blog post was engaging, a grassroots user could make the Hot Read list. As long as they could attract more followers, they could also make the Hot Visit and Fan lists.

Xie Yang continued, "An employee of mine has mentioned Witkey several times. I've studied the Witkey model in detail and think it's a very good development project. Our current product lineup is still too limited, and a well-run Witkey platform can be very profitable."

Witkey, what a distant term.

Chen Guiliang had almost forgotten about it.

To put it simply, employers post tasks with bounties, Witkeys bid on them, and the website takes a commission from the transaction. The tasks could be as small as designing a logo or as large as an outsourcing project worth hundreds of thousands of yuan.

The only one who truly made it big with Witkey was Zhubajie.com.

This website might not seem very famous, but over a decade later, its market value would grow to tens of billions of yuan.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Are you planning to build it yourself?"

Xie Yang said, "Of course we'll build it ourselves. The concept of Witkey was proposed last year. The existing Witkey websites are all in their infancy. It's better for us to build our own than to invest in them."

Chen Guiliang asked, "For the employers posting tasks, how do you guarantee their submissions won't be stolen? If a Witkey completes a task and the employer bails on the payment, what then? When many Witkeys bid on a task, only one gets paid, and the rest work for nothing. How do you maintain the Witkeys' motivation?"

"Uh..." Xie Yang didn't know how to answer.

Chen Guiliang said, "Establishing an effective intermediary guarantee and evaluation system requires a massive investment of manpower and resources. The person in charge of this project must also have a vast and powerful network of connections."

Xie Yang said, "I'll think about it some more."

After Xie Yang left, Chen Guiliang used "Zhubajie" for the website.

This website had already been founded!

But the webpage was very simple, likely still a personal website in its startup phase.

The contact information for business cooperation listed on the site included a mobile phone, QQ, MSN, and email.

Chen Guiliang logged into QQ and added the other party as a friend.

Little Boy Under the Streetlight: "Hello."

Zhubajie: "Hello. Are you looking to post a bounty task?"

Little Boy Under the Streetlight: "May I ask what you do? I'm afraid of getting scammed if I post a bounty."

Zhubajie: "My main job is as a chief reporter for the 'Shancheng Evening News.' If you have any doubts, you can come to the 'Shancheng Evening News' office to confirm in person."

It dawned on Chen Guiliang. No wonder this person could build a successful Witkey website. And his breakthrough method was to get CCTV's "Xinwen Lianbo" to report on it, which directly established its industry status and dispelled any customer doubts about it being a scam.

Who else would have such means and connections?

After the "Xinwen Lianbo" report, hundreds of Witkey websites sprung up in a short time. Apart from his Zhubajie.com, not a single one managed to grow big!

Little Boy Under the Streetlight: "Are you short on funds?"

Zhubajie: "???"

Little Boy Under the Streetlight: "Your site is currently a non-commercial personal website, so you can only take on small-time jobs. I can invest in you to officially establish a company and build a proper commercial website."

Zhubajie: "Are you a venture capital manager?"

Little Boy Under the Streetlight: "Something like that. Anyway, I have money that I don't know where to spend."

Zhubajie: "I need to talk to you in person."

Little Boy Under the Streetlight: "Sure. When are you free?"

Zhubajie: "Anytime. When you get to Shancheng, call the business contact number on the website. That's my mobile number."

He ended the QQ chat.

Chen Guiliang then called Bian Guanyue. "When are you going to the Super Girl competition?"

Bian Guanyue said, "I got a direct pass, straight into the top 100 of the Rongcheng division. I'm going back to Rongcheng this weekend for the 100-to-50 advancement competition."

"Amazing!" Chen Guiliang exclaimed.

Bian Guanyue laughed, "It's nothing, just making it to the top 100 of a regional division."

Chen Guiliang asked, "How far can you go in the competition without signing a contract? Have you looked into it?"

"I have," Bian Guanyue said. "This weekend's competition will probably be my last. Everyone who makes it to the top 50 in the regional divisions has to sign a contract."

Chen Guiliang couldn't help but laugh. "Hunan TV and EE-Media are being too cautious, making all the top 50 from every division sign contracts."
